description: This Java source file defines the TcpConnector class which manages TCP socket connections for a specific protocol, including establishing a connection, sending data, and handling responses within a networked application.

classes.name: TcpConnector
classes.description: A class responsible for establishing and managing TCP connections to a specified host and port, including sending commands and reading responses.

classes.name: InvalidTcpPort
classes.description: A nested static exception class used internally to signal invalid port inputs.

methods.name: TcpConnector
methods.description: Constructor that initializes the TCP connector with a specified port string, parsing the port number and hostname.

methods.name: isTcpPort
methods.description: Checks whether a given port string is valid for TCP connection.

methods.name: getTcpPort
methods.description: Parses and returns the port number from a string, expecting format like 'hostname:port' or 'port'.

methods.name: getHostname
methods.description: Extracts the hostname from the port string or defaults to 'localhost'.

methods.name: connect
methods.description: Establishes a blocking TCP connection to the specified host and port, sets up data listeners, and initiates protocol communication.

methods.name: restart
methods.description: Placeholder method for restarting the connection, currently empty.

methods.name: hasError
methods.description: Indicates if the connector has errors; currently always returns false.

methods.name: unpack
methods.description: Returns the input packet as-is; placeholder for potential message processing.

methods.name: send
methods.description: Sends a command string over the TCP connection using the binary protocol handler.

methods.name: getAvailablePorts
methods.description: Returns a list with the default TCP port if the port is open, otherwise an empty list.

methods.name: isTcpPortOpened
methods.description: Checks if the default port is open and accepting connections on localhost.
